Fixed anchors: A = solid curved service counter and customer-side stool row; B = kitchen hatch at rear end; C = coffee equipment/back worktop on staff side; D = windows, booths and entrance on customer side. Side labels refer to these physical features, not screen direction.

People tracked: W = gray-haired waitress, blue shirt, white apron, hair in bun; M = gray-haired customer, brown jacket and dark trousers. Additional W instance tracked separately when simultaneously visible.
State shot 1: W/M not reliably identifiable through distant glazing; A/B/C visible only at small scale, D establishes exterior/interior boundary; facing/action indeterminate.
State shot 2: W present on staff side of A between A and C, in front of B and opposite D; faces countertop, wipes with right hand and walks along work aisle. M not visible.

State shot 3: W remains staff-side A near C, facing customer aisle, stops wiping and lifts coffee pot. M enters view near B, visibly rounds far end of A into D-side aisle, walks along stools and sits facing W; his route is shown.

State shot 4: W partially visible on C/staff side of A, pouring with right hand; M's brown-sleeved hands remain on D/customer side around mug, then withdraw. B blurred behind; D cropped. Bodies and full facing directions cropped.
State shot 5: W/M outside food-insert framing; A supports plate, D booths behind it; B/C cropped. Person absence cannot be inferred from this crop.

State shot 6: M present at curved end of A, facing camera, both hands holding mug; torso lies beyond tabletop toward C while legs emerge on stool/customer side beneath solid counter fascia. B remains behind him and D opposite. W not visible.

State shot 7: W present at diner-facing sill of B, on staff side of A with C beside her; wipes with right hand, turns toward M, then resumes. M remains seated at distant curved A end toward entrance/D, holding mug. Reverse camera explains screen-side changes.
State shot 8: W/M not visible in framed portion of A/B/C; D-side light changes from cool to warm during empty-room hold, supporting elapsed time rather than a continuous-action disappearance.

State shot 9: M present on D/customer side of A, seated near B end, facing C and looking down at mug. W present between A and C, initially facing equipment, then turns and walks toward M/B with dishes.

State shot 10: M stays customer-side A, with D behind him and B behind his far shoulder; holds/lifts mug and looks toward W. W stays staff-side A in front of C, handles plate and mug, then turns toward B carrying plate.

State shot 11: M stays seated customer-side A facing C. W starts staff-side near B, visibly moves around far end of A, then sits on adjacent customer stool nearer B; both face C with D behind them. No through-counter crossing is established here.

State shot 12: W/M remain beside each other on D/customer side of A, W nearer B end and M nearer curved end; both hold mugs, M turns toward W. C is behind camera; B mostly cropped. Reversed screen ordering agrees with camera reversal.
State shot 13: W/M not visible in A/B/C view; strong sun and empty-room insert support a temporal transition. Their exact former seats are not both established within this crop.

State shot 14: hands enter countertop crop, place cash beside mug, then withdraw; at least one brown cuff supports M attribution. Full bodies, facing and positions relative to B/C/D are unobservable; no cross-cut hand substitution established.

State shot 15: M outside D/window plane, back toward camera, walking toward truck cab. W visible as reflection from inside D, facing outward; A/B/C cropped. Reflection is not a second physical waitress.
State shot 16: W physically inside D beside booths, facing truck, then turning away; her reflection remains in glass. M outside D at cab, reaches/opening door. A/B/C cropped.

State shot 17: W initially seated on D/customer side of A facing C, rises with dishes, then moves directly through solid A into staff aisle by C. A second matching W is simultaneously visible near B end wiping A; original W then walks toward her. M not visible, consistent with departure.
Diff shots 1-3: exterior-to-interior reveal does not establish disappearance; W keeps staff-side placement, and M's entry and route around counter end are visible.
Diff shots 3-5: coffee insert preserves person/action ownership; food insert crops people and implies service progression, so no missing-person finding.

Diff shots 5-7, also against shot 3: shot 6 places M through solid counter geometry; elapsed time could explain service changes but cannot explain that intersection. Shot 7 reverses camera and preserves M at counter end.
Diff shots 7-9: empty-room/daybreak passage permits W/M relocation before daylight wide; no unsupported instantaneous disappearance finding.

Diff shots 9-12: same customer and staff counter sides persist until W visibly walks around far end to join M; reverse two-shot preserves their physical seating order. No duplicate or hand-owner switch.

Diff shots 12-16: sunlit empty-room and payment inserts allow elapsed time before departure; customer's outside movement continues across window angles. Waitress double image is explained by glass reflection.

Diff shots 16-17: cut to W seated can represent elapsed time; within shot 17, however, direct passage through A and two simultaneous matching W bodies are visible, without a cut or reflective surface explaining them.

findings.description: After the food insert, the frontal wide at 00:36.458 places the customer's torso behind the tabletop toward the equipment wall while his trousered legs emerge on the customer side below its solid front. The continuous countertop and fascia pass across his seated waist/hip position; he is embedded in the counter rather than seated beside its stool-side edge. This persists through 00:44 and cannot be explained by camera reversal or elapsed time.

After rising from the customer-side stool, the waitress moves directly toward the equipment wall. Around 01:52.25-01:52.75 her hips and legs cross the solid countertop/fascia into the staff aisle while she carries dishes. She does not go around either counter end, and no opening exists along the visible crossing path; the camera remains continuous.

As the foreground waitress rises and moves to the equipment wall, another matching gray-haired, blue-shirted, white-aproned waitress is revealed wiping the far counter near the kitchen hatch. Both bodies are simultaneously visible from about 01:52 through 01:55, performing different actions several metres apart in the same continuous view. The second figure occupies the physical counter area, not window glass or a mirror, unlike the earlier explained reflections.
